claims.claim: Epiphanius of Salamis was bishop of Salamis, Cyprus, and lived approximately from c. 310–320 to 403 CE.
Epiphanius was born near Eleutheropolis in Palestine and was elected bishop of Salamis (Constantia) in 367, serving for nearly forty years until his death.

The work De prophetarum vita et obitu (Recensio altera) is attributed to Epiphanius of Salamis but is part of a collection of texts with disputed authorship, with some versions attributed to Epiphanius, others to Dorotheus of Tyre, and an anonymous recension also existing.
The Recensio altera of De prophetarum vita et obitu was composed in the fourth century.

The work survives in Greek manuscripts, with Codex Coisl. 120 (tenth century) being the leading representative of the shorter recension attributed to Epiphanius, while Codex Paris. Gr. 1115 (copied in 1276) is the chief witness for the longer recension attributed to Epiphanius.
The text was edited by Theodor Schermann and published in Leipzig by B. G. Teubneri in 1907 as part of Prophetarum vitae fabulosae, appearing in columns 393–414 of Patrologia Graeca volume 43.
The work provides brief accounts of the lives, origins, and deaths of the prophets, including details such as their tribal affiliations and places of burial.
